title: Bekhorot 7
description: Does Rabbi Shimon require a camel born to a cow to resemble its mother in head and most of its body before it may be eaten, Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua on a lamb with a non-kosher father, then what a non-kosher creature produces: a donkey’s urine, bees’ honey, a deer’s discharges, a newborn’s facial skin, and a fish found inside a fish.
topics: 🐪 A camel born to a cow: for eating, does Rabbi Shimon require its head and most of its body to resemble its mother?
🐑 “Seh kesavim veseh izzim”: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Eliezer on a lamb whose father is not kosher
🔄 “This and that cause”: why each Tanna seems to reverse himself on a tereifa’s offspring
🐴 Is a donkey’s urine like its milk? Rav Sheshet: “from the non-kosher”
🍯 Why bees’ honey is permitted: Rabbi Ya’akov’s verse, and the honey of gizzin and wasps
🦌 A fallow deer’s discharge, and the skin over a newborn donkey’s face
🐟 A kosher fish found inside a non-kosher fish: swallowed or spawned?

a1.he: אִישְׁתַּנִּי מִגָּמָל שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי, אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא שְׁנָא?

a2.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה — אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה, וְאִם דּוֹמֶה רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ לְאִמּוֹ — חַיָּיב בִּבְכוֹרָה. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: לַאֲכִילָה נָמֵי בָּעֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ!

a3.he: לָא, לִבְכוֹרָה דַּוְקָא. דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָא שָׁבְקַהּ לַאֲכִילָה וְקָם לֵיהּ אַבְּכוֹר. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: לִבְכוֹרָה הוּא דְּבָעֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ, אֲבָל לַאֲכִילָה — לָא.

a4.he: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ: לַאֲכִילָה נָמֵי בָּעֵי, וּבְכוֹרָה אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״אַךְ בְּכוֹר שׁוֹר״, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר, וְלֹא תִּיסְגֵּי לֵיהּ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ עַד דְּאִיכָּא כּוּלֵּיהּ, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן.

a5.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״אַךְ אֶת זֶה לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מִמַּעֲלֵי הַגֵּרָה וּמִמַּפְרִיסֵי הַפַּרְסָה״, זֶה — אִי אַתָּה אוֹכֵל, אֲבָל אַתָּה אוֹכֵל הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד.

a6.he: וְאִי זֶה זֶה הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד? זֶה טָמֵא הַנּוֹלָד מִן הַטָּהוֹר, וְעִבּוּרוֹ מִן הַטָּהוֹר.

a7.he: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ עִבּוּרוֹ מִן הַטָּמֵא? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״שֵׂה כְשָׂבִים וְשֵׂה עִזִּים״, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא אָבִיו כֶּבֶשׂ וְאִמּוֹ כִּבְשָׂה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.

a8.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא בָּא הַכָּתוּב לְהַתִּיר אֶת הַמּוּתָּר, אֶלָּא לְהוֹסִיף עַל הַמּוּתָּר, וְאֵיזֶה זֶה? טָמֵא הַנּוֹלָד מִן הַטָּהוֹר וְעִבּוּרוֹ מִן הַטָּמֵא. אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עִבּוּרוֹ מִן הַטָּהוֹר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״שׁוֹר שֵׂה כְשָׂבִים וְשֵׂה עִזִּים״ מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.

a9.he: קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״טָמֵא״, כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְקָאָמַר: אֲבָל אַתָּה אוֹכֵל הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד!

a10.he: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא.

a11.he: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַקְשֵׁי וּמוֹתֵיב: עִבּוּרוֹ מִן הַטָּמֵא — מִי מִעַבְּרָא?

a12.he: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: לְעוֹלָם אֵין מִתְעַבֶּרֶת לֹא טְמֵאָה מִן הַטָּהוֹר, וְלֹא טְהוֹרָה מִן הַטָּמֵא, וְלֹא גַּסָּה מִן הַדַּקָּה, וְלֹא דַּקָּה מִן הַגַּסָּה, וְלֹא בְּהֵמָה מִן חַיָּה, וְלֹא חַיָּה מִן בְּהֵמָה.

a13.he: חוּץ מֵרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וּמַחְלוּקְתּוֹ, שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים חַיָּה מִתְעַבֶּרֶת מִבְּהֵמָה!

a14.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: דְּאִיעַבַּר מִקָּלוּט בֶּן פָּרָה, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קָאָמַר, וְקָאָמַר: אֲבָל אַתָּה אוֹכֵל הַבָּא בְּסִימָן אֶחָד!

a15.he: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא.

a16.he: לְמֵימְרָא, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם — מוּתָּר, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם — אָסוּר?

a17.he: וְהָא אִיפְּכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לְהוּ: וְלַד טְרֵיפָה, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא יִקְרַב לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יִקְרַב לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ!

a18.he: בְּעָלְמָא סָבַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם — אָסוּר, וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא, דְּאִם כֵּן נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא: ״שֵׂה כְשָׂבִים וְעִזִּים״, ״שֵׂה״ ״וְשֵׂה״ לְמָה לִי? שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: שֶׂה — מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.

a19.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר לְךָ: בְּעָלְמָא זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם — מוּתָּר, וְהָכָא אִם כֵּן לִכְתּוֹב קְרָא: ״שׁוֹר כֶּשֶׂב וָעֵז״, ״כְּשָׂבִים וְעִזִּים״ לְמָה לִי? שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא אָבִיו כֶּבֶשׂ וְאִמּוֹ כִּבְשָׂה.

a20.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, ״גָּמָל״ ״גָּמָל״ שְׁנֵי פְּעָמִים — אֶחָד גָּמָל הַנּוֹלָד מִן הַגָּמָל, וְאֶחָד גָּמָל הַנּוֹלָד מִן הַפָּרָה, וְאִם רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְאִמּוֹ — מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה.

a21.he: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, לַאֲכִילָה נָמֵי בָּעֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

a22.he: שֶׁהַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַטָּמֵא וְכוּ׳. בְּעוֹ מִינַּהּ מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מֵי רַגְלַיִם שֶׁל חֲמוֹר, מַהוּ?

a23.he: וְתִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ דְּסוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים? דְּסוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ, דְּלָא עֲכִירִי וְלָא דָּמוּ לְחָלָב, מַיָּא עוּל מַיָּא נְפוּק. כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ דַּחֲמוֹר, דַּעֲכִירִי וְדָמוּ לְחָלָב, מַאי? מִגּוּפֵיהּ קָא מִימַּצְצִי וַאֲסִירִי, אוֹ דִלְמָא מַיָּא עוּל מַיָּא נְפוּק, וְהַאי דַּעֲכִירִי — הַבְלָא דְּבִישְׂרָא הוּא?

a24.he: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, תְּנֵיתוּה: שֶׁהַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַטָּמֵא — טָמֵא, וְהַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַטָּהוֹר — טָהוֹר. ״מִטָּמֵא״ לָא קָאָמַר, אֶלָּא ״מִן

b1.he: הַטָּמֵא״, וְהָנֵי נָמֵי מִינָא דְּטָמֵא הוּא.

b2.he: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, דְּסוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ, דְּלָא שָׁתוּ אִינָשֵׁי. כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ דַּחֲמוֹר, דְּשָׁתוּ אִינָשֵׁי וּמְעַלּוּ לְיַרְקוֹנָא, מַאי?

b3.he: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, תְּנֵיתוּהָ: הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַטָּמֵא טָמֵא, וְהַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַטָּהוֹר טָהוֹר — וְהָנֵי נָמֵי מִטָּמֵא קָאָתֵי.

b4.he: מֵיתִיבִי: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ דְּבַשׁ דְּבוֹרִים מוּתָּר? מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּכְנִיסוֹת אוֹתוֹ לְגוּפָן, וְאֵין מְמַצּוֹת אוֹתוֹ מִגּוּפָן.

b5.he: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב, דְּאָמַר: דּוּבְשָׁא רַחֲמָנָא שַׁרְיֵיהּ.

b6.he: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: ״אַךְ אֶת זֶה תֹּאכְלוּ מִכֹּל שֶׁרֶץ הָעוֹף״ — זֶה אַתָּה אוֹכֵל, וְאִי אַתָּה אוֹכֵל שֶׁרֶץ עוֹף טָמֵא.

b7.he: שֶׁרֶץ עוֹף טָמֵא בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב! אֶלָּא שֶׁרֶץ עוֹף טָמֵא אִי אַתָּה אוֹכֵל, אֲבָל אַתָּה אוֹכֵל מַה שֶּׁעוֹף טָמֵא מַשְׁרִיץ, וְאֵיזֶה זֶה? זֶה דְּבַשׁ דְּבוֹרִים.

b8.he: יָכוֹל אַף דְּבַשׁ הַגַּזִּין וְהַצִּירְעִין? אָמַרְתָּ: לֹא. וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת דְּבוֹרִים, וּלְהוֹצִיא הַגַּזִּין וְהַצִּירְעִין? מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי דְּבַשׁ דְּבוֹרִים שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שֵׁם לְוַוי, וּמוֹצִיא אֲנִי דְּבַשׁ הַגַּזִּין וְהַצִּירְעִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם לְוַוי.

b9.he: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא: דְּבַשׁ הַגַּזִּין וְהַצִּירְעִין טָהוֹר וּמוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה? דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב.

b10.he: טָהוֹר — אַלְמָא בָּעֵי מַחְשָׁבָה. תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: דְּבַשׁ בְּכַוַּורְתּוֹ מְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֳוכָלִין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמַחְשָׁבָה.

b11.he: חָלֵי דְּיַחְמוּרְתָּא, סְבוּר רַבָּנַן לְמֵימַר: בֵּיעֵי נִינְהוּ וַאֲסִירָן. אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: זַרְעָא דְּאַיָּלָא הוּא, דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר אַיָּלְתָּא, וְאַיְּידֵי דְּרַחְמָהּ צַר לָא מִזְדַּקְקָא, וְאָזֵיל בָּתַר יַחְמוּרְתָּא וְנָתְרִי.

b12.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: עוֹר הַבָּא כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל חֲמוֹר — מוּתָּר, מַאי טַעְמָא? פִּירְשָׁא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא.

b13.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: תַּנְיָא דִּמְסַיַּע לָךְ: עוֹר הַבָּא כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם, בֵּין חַי בֵּין מֵת — טָהוֹר. מַאי לָאו בֵּין הוּא חַי וְאִמּוֹ חַיָּה, בֵּין הוּא מֵת וְאִמּוֹ מֵתָה?

b14.he: לָא, בֵּין הוּא חַי וְאִמּוֹ מֵתָה, בֵּין הוּא מֵת וְאִמּוֹ חַיָּה. וְהָתַנְיָא: בֵּין הוּא חַי וְאִמּוֹ חַיָּה, בֵּין הוּא מֵת וְאִמּוֹ מֵתָה! אִי תַּנְיָא, תַּנְיָא.

b15.he: מַתְנִי׳ דָּג טָמֵא שֶׁבָּלַע דָּג טָהוֹר, מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה, וְטָהוֹר שֶׁבָּלַע דָּג טָמֵא, אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ גִּידּוּלוֹ.

b16.he: גְּמָ׳ טַעְמָא דַּחֲזֵינֵיהּ דִּבְלַע, הָא לָא חֲזֵינֵיהּ דִּבְלַע — אָמְרִי: אַשְׁרוֹצֵי אַשְׁרֵיץ.

b17.he: מְנָלַן? דְּתַנְיָא: דָּג טָמֵא מַשְׁרִיץ, דָּג טָהוֹר מֵטִיל בֵּיצִים. אִי הָכִי, כִּי חָזֵינָא דִּבְלַע אָמְרִינַן: הַאי אִיעַכַּלָא, וְהַאי אַשְׁרוֹצֵי אַשְׁרֵיץ!

b18.he: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּצָאוֹ דֶּרֶךְ הָרֶיעִי. רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּצָאוֹ דֶּרֶךְ בֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה. רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּצָאוֹ שָׁלֵם.

b19.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רוֹב דָּגִים בְּמִינָן מַשְׁרִיצִין, וּכְמִי שֶׁבָּלַע לְפָנֵינוּ דָּמֵי.

b20.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: דָּג טָמֵא — מַשְׁרִיץ, דָּג טָהוֹר — מֵטִיל בֵּיצִים, כָּל הַמּוֹלִיד — מֵנִיק, וְכׇל הַמֵּטִיל בֵּיצִים — מְלַקֵּט, חוּץ מֵעֲטַלֵּף שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּטִיל בֵּיצִים — מֵנִיק.

messages.text: 7a

Continued from 6b: Rabbi Shimon requires a firstborn’s head and most of its body to resemble its mother. The Gemara asked whether he requires the same for eating a non-kosher animal born to a kosher one: perhaps the Merciful One forbids only an ordinary camel, but if…

…it is different from an ordinary camel and has some characteristics of its mother, perhaps it is permitted to eat it. Or perhaps there is no difference, and with regard to consumption Rabbi Shimon also requires that its head and the majority of its body resemble its mother.

notes.he: שדומה לאמו במקצת סימנין:
notes.en: It differs from a camel: in that it resembles its mother in some of its signs.

messages.text: Come and hear a proof from a baraita:

With regard to a kosher animal that gave birth to a non-kosher animal of sorts, the offspring is forbidden for consumption, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon; but if its head and the majority of its body are similar to its mother, it is obligated in, i.e., subject to the obligations of, firstborn status.

notes.dh: ת"ש בהמה טהורה שילדה מין בהמה טמאה אסור באכילה
notes.he: הא ברייתא ר' שמעון היא דאיהו אמר דאסור באכילה וקתני אם דומה ראשו ורובו לאמו חייב בבכורה ש"מ דה"ה נמי לאכילה בעי ר' שמעון ראשו ורובו לא לבכורה דוקא כלל:
notes.en: Come and hear: a kosher animal that gave birth to a non-kosher kind is forbidden for consumption. This baraita is Rabbi Shimon’s, for he is the one who says it is forbidden for consumption; and it teaches: if its head and the majority of its body resemble its mother it is obligated in firstborn status. Learn from it that the same is true for consumption: Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body, not only for firstborn status.

messages.text: Learn from it that with regard to consumption, Rabbi Shimon also requires that its head and the majority of its body resemble the mother.

notes.he: ומאן שמעת ליה הך סברא ר"ש ואם ראשו ורובו כו' וקס"ד דמדקתני להו בהדי הדדי ש"מ דאפי' לאכילה בעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו:
notes.en: Is forbidden for consumption: and whom have you heard holding this view? Rabbi Shimon. [It then teaches:] “And if its head and the majority of its body…” And it was assumed that since it teaches the two together, learn from it that even for consumption Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body.

notes.dh: שמע מינה לאכילה נמי בעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו
notes.he: דמשמע שאין בו כי אם שני חלוקין מדלא קתני חלוק שלישי ולימא אם יש בו מקצת סימנין מותר באכילה והדר ליתני ואם ראשו ורובו דומה לאמו חייב בבכורה והשתא רישא וסיפא רבותא קמשמע לן דרישא קתני שילדה מין טמאה דאסור אף באכילה וסיפא דקתני ראשו ורובו דומים לאמו חייב אף בבכורה:
notes.en: Learn from it that for consumption too Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body: for it implies that there are only two categories [in the baraita], since it does not teach a third category, saying: If it has some of the signs it is permitted for consumption, and then teach: And if its head and the majority of its body resemble its mother it is obligated in firstborn status. As it stands, both the first clause and the latter clause teach a novelty: the first clause teaches that [a kosher animal] gave birth to a non-kosher kind, which is forbidden even for consumption, and the latter clause teaches that if its head and the majority of its body resemble its mother, it is obligated even in firstborn status.

messages.text: No, the requirement that its head and the majority of its body resemble the mother is relevant specifically with regard to firstborn status.
messages.quote: it is obligated in firstborn status

messages.text: The language of the baraita is also precise, as the tanna leaves the halakha of consumption with which he began and addresses the halakha of firstborn status. Learn from it that it is with regard to firstborn status that Rabbi Shimon requires that its head and the majority of its body resemble the mother, but with regard to consumption he does not require this, and even a partial similarity suffices.

notes.he: דאיירי ברישא וקם ליה אבכורה ולא אמר אם ראשו ורובו דומה לאמו מותר באכילה ש"מ לאכילה סגי במקצת סימנין:
notes.en: Since it leaves consumption: which it discussed in the first clause, and turns to firstborn status, and does not say: If its head and the majority of its body resemble its mother it is permitted for consumption, learn from it that for consumption some of the signs suffice.

messages.text: Actually, I will say to you that with regard to the permissibility of consumption he also requires that its head and the majority of its body be similar to the mother. But it was necessary to state this condition specifically with regard to the halakha of firstborn status, as it might enter your mind to say that since it is written: “But the firstborn of an ox”, perhaps firstborn status does not apply unless it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox, and a resemblance of the offspring’s head and the majority of its body to the mother does not suffice unless its whole body has the appearance of an ox. Therefore, the tanna teaches us that a resemblance of its head and the majority of its body to the mother do suffice.

verse.he: אַךְ בְּכוֹר־שׁוֹר אוֹ־בְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב אוֹ־בְכוֹר עֵז לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם אֶת־דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת־חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But the firstlings of cattle, sheep, or goats may not be redeemed; they are consecrated. You shall dash their blood against the altar, and turn their fat into smoke as an offering by fire for a pleasing odor to GOD.

notes.he: ולעולם בתרוייהו בעינן ראשו ורובו:
notes.en: It was necessary for firstborn status: but actually, for both we require its head and the majority of its body.

messages.text: Come and hear a proof from a baraita:

The Torah states: “Nevertheless these shall you not eat from them that only chew the cud, or from them that only have a split hoof: The camel”. The phrase: “From them that only chew the cud,” which is referring to animals that are forbidden for consumption, indicates that a camel or other non-kosher animal that is born to a kosher animal is forbidden. Furthermore, the word “these” teaches that concerning these animals that resemble a non-kosher animal, you may not eat them when they are born to a kosher animal, but you may eat a non-kosher animal that comes with one characteristic of its mother.

verse.he: אַךְ אֶת־זֶה לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מִמַּעֲלֵי הַגֵּרָה וּמִמַּפְרִסֵי הַפַּרְסָה אֶת־הַגָּמָל כִּי־מַעֲלֵה גֵרָה הוּא וּפַרְסָה אֵינֶנּוּ מַפְרִיס טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם׃
verse.en: The following, however, of those that either chew the cud or have true hoofs, you shall not eat: the camel—although it chews the cud, it has no true hoofs: it is impure for you;

notes.he: גמל אפי' נולד מן הפרה:
notes.en: These you may not eat: a camel, even if it was born from a cow.

notes.dh: אבל אתה אוכל אחר הבא בסימן אחד
notes.he: של אמו כלומר שדומה לאמו במקצת כגון טמא שנולד מן הטהור ודומה לאמו במקצת:
notes.en: But you may eat another that comes with one sign: of its mother; that is, one that resembles its mother in part, such as a non-kosher animal born from a kosher one that resembles its mother in part.

notes.he: גמל ושפן כתיבי בקרא אבל אתה אוכל הבא בסימן אחד לאו בסימני טהרה איירי דממעלה גרה וממפריסי הפרסה אלא בדמי למקצת סימנין לאמו ביד וברגל ובצמרו (ולד) סימני טהרה בעי:
notes.en: These you may not eat: the camel and the hyrax are written in the verse. “But you may eat what comes with one sign” does not speak of the signs of kosher status, chewing the cud and having split hooves, but of resembling its mother in some features: in the forelegs, in the hind legs and in its wool. [To be kosher by its own] signs of kosher status, it requires [both of] the signs.

notes.he: זה אי אתה אוכל את הגמל וגו' אבל אתה אוכל הבא בסימן אחד דהיינו דאם יש בו מקצת סימן דומה:
notes.en: These you may not eat, the camel, etc., but you may eat what comes with one sign: that is, if it has some partial resemblance.

messages.text: And which animal is this that comes with one characteristic of its mother? This is a non-kosher animal that is born from a kosher female animal and its impregnation came from a kosher male animal.

One might have thought that even if its conception came from a non-kosher male animal it should be permitted. Therefore, the verse states: “These are the beasts which you may eat: “The ox, the sheep [seh kesavim], and goat [veseh izzim]”. The plural form of “kesavim” and “izzim” indicates that a lamb is not kosher unless its father is a male sheep and its mother is a female sheep. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua.

verse.he: זֹאת הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכֵלוּ שׁוֹר שֵׂה כְשָׂבִים וְשֵׂה עִזִּים׃
verse.en: These are the animals that you may eat: the ox, the sheep, and the goat;

notes.he: שה הבא משני כבשים:
notes.en: Seh kesavim: a seh [lamb] that comes from two sheep.

notes.he: מדכתיב כבשים ועזים ולא כתיב כבש ועז דרש ר' יהושע ור' אליעזר מדכתיב שה שה תרי זימני והשתא דרשות דר' יהושע לאסור לאו הוא דר"א להתיר ולשון לא בא הכתוב דאמר ר"א מגומגם קצת דמשמע הלשון דמקרא זה שדרש ר' יהושע טמא שנולד מן טהור ועיבורו מן הטהור אמר ר"א דבא להוסיף על המותר ולהתיר טמא הנולד מן הטהור ועיבורו מן הטמא ויש לפרש לא בא הכתוב כמו לא באתה התורה עוד י"ל דברי רבי אליעזר וה"פ משה שה נפקא לן עיבורו מן הטהור לכך אייתר זה להוסיף על המותר ועיבורו מן הטמא:
notes.en: Unless its father and its mother are sheep: Rabbi Yehoshua expounds this from the fact that it is written kesavim and izzim [in the plural], and not keves and ez, and Rabbi Eliezer from the fact that seh, seh is written twice. So the exposition Rabbi Yehoshua uses to forbid is not the one Rabbi Eliezer uses to permit. The phrase “the verse does not come,” which Rabbi Eliezer says, is somewhat awkward, for the wording implies that this very verse, which Rabbi Yehoshua expounded about a non-kosher animal born from a kosher one whose conception was from a kosher one, Rabbi Eliezer says comes to add to the permitted, permitting a non-kosher animal born from a kosher one whose conception was from a non-kosher one. One may explain “the verse does not come” like “the Torah did not come” [a general expression]. Alternatively, one may say this is the meaning of Rabbi Eliezer’s words: from “seh, seh” we derive [the case where] its conception was from a kosher animal; therefore “these” is left over to add to the permitted, [even where] its conception was from a non-kosher animal.

notes.he: ריבה עד שיהא אביו כבש ואמו כבשה:
notes.en: The verse states: “Seh kesavim and seh izzim.” It extends [the requirement]: until its father is a ram and its mother a ewe.

messages.text: Offspring whose father and mother are both kosher are permitted, and this verse which renders permitted an offspring that partially resembles its mother does not come to permit that which is permitted, i.e., where both parents are kosher, but it comes rather to add to that which is permitted; and which case is this? It is a case of a non-kosher animal that is born from a kosher animal and its conception came from a non-kosher animal.
messages.quote: unless its father is a male sheep and its mother is a female sheep

notes.he: דכיון דאביו ואמו טהורים לא איצטריך האי קרא דאך את זה תאכלו למישרייה:
notes.en: To permit the permitted: since its father and mother are kosher, this verse, “Yet these you may eat,” was not needed to permit it.

notes.dh: לא בא הכתוב להתיר את המותר
notes.he: כשיהא אביו נמי כבש אלא להוסיף על המותר ואיזה זה זה תאכלו:
notes.en: The verse does not come to permit the permitted: where its father too is a ram; rather, to add to the permitted. And which is this? “These you may eat.”

messages.text: Or perhaps it permits only an animal whose conception came from a kosher animal? The verse states: “The ox, the sheep [seh kesavim], and goat [veseh izzim].” The repetition of the word seh indicates that it is permitted to be eaten in any case, even if only its mother was a ewe.

notes.he: מדכתיב שה שה תרי זימני שמע מיניה דאפי' מצד האם ולא מצד האב:
notes.en: In any case: since seh is written twice, learn from it that [it is permitted] even [if it is a sheep] on its mother’s side and not on its father’s side.

notes.he: דבעי נמי קרא אלא עבורו על הטהור והיינו להוסיף על המותר להחמיר דולד הוי טמא ולעולם בעינן נמי קרא עיבורו מן הטהור ת"ל שה כשבים מכל מקום וכיון דאמו כבשה אע"ג דלאו אביו כבש:
notes.en: Or perhaps not: that the verse is needed only [where] its conception was from a kosher animal, and that “to add to the permitted” means to be stringent, since the offspring is non-kosher, and actually we still require that its conception be from a kosher animal? The verse states “seh kesavim”: in any case, since its mother is a ewe, even though its father is not a ram.

messages.text: In any event, the tanna of this baraita refers to a non-kosher animal that was born to a kosher animal as non-kosher, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who deems a camel that was born to a cow forbidden to eat, and he says: But you may eat a non-kosher animal that comes with one characteristic that is similar to its mother. Apparently, Rabbi Shimon does not require that the head and the majority of the body resemble the mother for it to be rendered fit for consumption.
messages.quote: but you may eat a non-kosher animal that comes with one characteristic

notes.he: לקלוט שנולד מן הטהור:
notes.en: He calls it non-kosher: the animal with closed hooves [kalut] that was born from a kosher one.

notes.he: דאסר ליה היכא דאין בו מקצת סימנין וקאמר דאם יש לו סימן אחד של טהרה שדומה לאמו במקצת מותר:
notes.en: In accordance with Rabbi Shimon: who forbids it where it does not have some of the signs; and he says that if it has one sign of kosher status, resembling its mother in part, it is permitted.

notes.he: כלומר מדקתני בהאי לישנא ואיזה זה זה טמא שנולד מן הטהור ולא קתני זה היוצא מן הטהור ש"מ דלר' שמעון קאמר דלר' שמעון הוי טמא גמור וקאמר אבל אתה אוכל בסימן אחד היינו מקצת סימן וש"מ דלא בעי ראשו ורובו:
notes.en: He calls it non-kosher, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon: that is, since it teaches in this language, “And which is this? This is a non-kosher animal born from a kosher one,” and does not teach “this is what emerges from a kosher one,” learn from it that it speaks according to Rabbi Shimon, for whom it is fully non-kosher. And it says, “but you may eat [what comes] with one sign,” that is, a partial sign. Learn from it that he does not require its head and the majority of its body.

messages.text: No proof may be brought from here, as this tanna holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon with regard to one matter, where a kosher animal gave birth to a non-kosher animal, maintaining that it is forbidden, and disagrees with his opinion with regard to one other matter, where the animal has some characteristics of the mother, in which case this tanna deems it permitted to be eaten. Concerning the second matter, Rabbi Shimon deems it forbidden unless the head and majority of the body resemble the mother.

notes.he: דר' שמעון בעי ראשו ורובו:
notes.en: And disagrees with him on one: for Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body.

notes.dh: האי תנא סבר ליה כותיה בחדא
notes.he: שטמא שנולד מן הטהור טמא:
notes.en: This tanna holds like him on one: that a non-kosher animal born from a kosher one is non-kosher.

notes.he: דאילו ר' שמעון סבר דאינו מותר באכילה עד שיהא ראשו ורובו דומה לאמו כדאמרינן גבי בכורה והאי תנא סבר אפילו מקצת סימן שרי באכילה:
notes.en: And disagrees with him on one: for Rabbi Shimon holds that it is not permitted for consumption unless its head and the majority of its body resemble its mother, as we said with regard to firstborn status, while this tanna holds that even a partial sign permits it for consumption.

messages.text: There are those who raise a difficulty with this baraita and resolve it, thereby resolving the dilemma concerning the opinion of Rabbi Shimon:

notes.he: קושיא להך ברייתא ומתוך הקושיא משיב דבר לשואל אי בעי ר' שמעון ראשו ורובו לאכילה או לא:
notes.en: And there are those who raise a difficulty: a difficulty against this baraita, and from within the difficulty one answers the questioner [on the dilemma] whether Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body for consumption or not.

notes.he: לברייתא ומותיב ומן פירוקא דמפרק מיפשט בעיין:
notes.en: And there are those who raise a difficulty: against the baraita, and they object, and from the resolution with which it is resolved, our dilemma is resolved.

messages.text: The baraita states that the kosher animal’s impregnation came from a non-kosher animal. Can a kosher animal become pregnant from a non-kosher animal?
messages.quote: its conception came from a non-kosher animal

notes.he: טהורה מטמא דקתני ועבורו מן הטמא:
notes.en: Does it become pregnant: [can] a kosher animal [become pregnant] from a non-kosher one, as it teaches, “and its conception was from a non-kosher animal”?

messages.text: A non-kosher animal never becomes pregnant from a kosher one, e.g., a camel from an ox, nor a kosher animal from a non-kosher one, e.g., a cow from a horse, nor a large animal from a small animal, e.g., a cow from a goat, nor a small one from a large one, e.g., a ewe from an ox, nor a domesticated animal from an undomesticated animal, e.g., a goat from a deer, nor an undomesticated animal from a domesticated animal, e.g., a gazelle from a goat.
messages.lead: But doesn’t Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:

messages.text: With regard to all these cases, everyone agrees that pregnancy is impossible except for Rabbi Eliezer and his disputants, who would say that an undomesticated animal can become pregnant from a domesticated animal (see Ḥullin 79b). Those Sages disagree with regard to whether slaughtering the offspring of a gazelle that became pregnant from a goat is included in the prohibition against slaughtering a mother and its offspring on the same day.

notes.he: שחולקין בכוי בפ' אותו ואת בנו בשחיטת חולין (דף עט:) אם אותו ואת בנו נוהג בו וקתני כוי הבא מן התייש ומן הצבייה אלמא חיה מתעברת מבהמה לדבריהם:
notes.en: Except for Rabbi Eliezer and his disputants: who disagree about the koy in chapter Oto Ve’et Beno in Sheḥitat Ḥullin (79b), whether [the prohibition of slaughtering] it and its offspring [on one day] applies to it; and it teaches there that a koy comes from a he-goat and a female gazelle. Evidently, according to them, an undomesticated animal becomes pregnant from a domesticated one.

notes.he: הא דלא קאמר חוץ מן הדולפנין שפרים ורבים מבני אדם כדאמר לקמן לא קשה מידי דלא איירי רבי יהושע בן לוי אלא בבהמה וחיה ולא בבני אדם והנהו בני ימא נינהו:
notes.en: Except for Rabbi Eliezer and his disputants: that he does not say “except for the dulfanin, which reproduce from people,” as is said below [8a], is no difficulty at all, for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi speaks only of domesticated and undomesticated animals, not of people, and those are creatures of the sea.

messages.text: When the baraita discusses the case of a kosher animal that became pregnant from a non-kosher animal, the reference is to a case where the kosher animal became pregnant from an animal with closed hooves that is the offspring of a cow. A cow can become pregnant from such an animal because the mother of that animal was a cow.

notes.he: האי עבורו מן הטמא דקאמר היינו שנתעברה מן הקלוט שפרסותיו קלוטות כגמל ובן פרה הוא ואליבא דר' שמעון קרי ליה טמא ובנו מותר אם דומה לאמו בסימן אחד אלמא לאכילה לא בעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yirmeya says: this “its conception was from a non-kosher animal” that it says means that it became pregnant from a kalut, whose hooves are closed like a camel’s, and which is the offspring of a cow. In accordance with Rabbi Shimon he calls it non-kosher, and its offspring is permitted if it resembles its mother in one sign. Evidently, for consumption Rabbi Shimon does not require its head and the majority of its body.

notes.he: גבי כוי כדאמר איזהו כוי שנחלקו בו ר' אליעזר וחכמים זה תיש הבא על הצביה אבל שאר רבנן לא אמרי דמיעברא ומפריק מאי עיבורו מן הטמא לא טמא ממש אלא א"ר ירמיה דאיעבר מקלוט שאין פרסות סדוקות בן פרה. ומדקרי להאי קלוט טמא דאמר היינו עיבורו מן הטמא ש"מ כר' שמעון קאמר דטמא היוצא מן הטהור טמא וקאמר אבל אתה אוכל הבא בסימן א' ש"מ דלא בעי ר' שמעון ראשו ורובו דומה לאמו לעולם בעי והאי תנא סבר לה כוותיה בחדא וכו' כדאמרינן מעיקרא:
notes.en: Except for Rabbi Eliezer and his disputants: regarding the koy, as it says: What is the koy about which Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis disagree? It is a he-goat that mated with a female gazelle. But the other Rabbis do not say that it becomes pregnant. And it resolves: what is “its conception from a non-kosher animal”? Not truly non-kosher; rather, Rabbi Yirmeya said: it became pregnant from a kalut, whose hooves are not split, the offspring of a cow. And since it calls this kalut non-kosher, saying this is “its conception from a non-kosher animal,” learn from it that it speaks according to Rabbi Shimon, that a non-kosher animal that comes from a kosher one is non-kosher; and it says, “but you may eat what comes with one sign”; learn from it that Rabbi Shimon does not require its head and the majority of its body to resemble its mother. [The Gemara answers:] Actually, he does require it, and this tanna holds like him on one, etc., as we said at first.

messages.text: And the tanna of the baraita said his opinion in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, that a non-kosher animal that was born from a kosher animal is considered non-kosher, and he says: But you may eat that which comes with one characteristic of its mother. Apparently, Rabbi Shimon does deem permitted the consumption of an animal with some characteristics similar to its mother.

This tanna holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon with regard to one matter, where a kosher animal gave birth to a non-kosher animal, maintaining that it is forbidden, and disagrees with his opinion with regard to one other matter, where the animal has some characteristics of the mother, in which case this tanna deems it fit for consumption. Concerning the second matter, Rabbi Shimon deems it forbidden unless the head and majority of the body resemble the mother.

notes.he: מה שיוכל לדחות דחי כן משום דבמסקנא לאכילה פשטינן נמי דבעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו:
notes.en: And disagrees with him on one: what it can deflect, it deflects in this way, because in the conclusion we resolve that for consumption too Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body.

messages.text: § Is this to say that Rabbi Eliezer holds that when both this and that cause it, i.e., both permitted and forbidden items contribute to a result, the result is permitted, and he therefore permits the consumption of the offspring of a kosher animal that became pregnant from a non-kosher animal; and Rabbi Yehoshua holds that when both this and that cause it, it is forbidden?
messages.quote: it is permitted to be eaten in any case

notes.he: ההיתר והאיסור גורמין לזה שיבא הוא טמא ואמו טהורה:
notes.en: This and that cause: the permitted and the forbidden [parent together] cause this one to come about, it being non-kosher and its mother kosher.

notes.he: מאי דר' אליעזר דשרי עבורו מן הטמא משום דסבר כיון דאמו טהורה אע"ג דאביו טמא כיון דזה וזה גורם הולד יש בו הגרמה דטהור ומותר:
notes.en: Is this to say: that Rabbi Eliezer permits [an offspring whose] conception was from a non-kosher animal because he holds that since its mother is kosher, even though its father is non-kosher, since “this and that cause,” the offspring has in it a kosher cause and is permitted?

notes.dh: ור' יהושע סבר זה וזה גורם אסור
notes.he: עד שיהא אביו ואמו טהורים דהגורמים שניהם טהורים:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehoshua holds that “this and that cause” is forbidden: unless its father and its mother are kosher, so that both causes are kosher.

messages.text: But we have heard them saying the opposite: With regard to the offspring of an animal with a wound that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa] and is forbidden to be eaten or sacrificed as an offering upon the altar:

notes.he: ואביו תמים הרי זה וזה גורם:
notes.en: The offspring of a tereifa: and its father is unblemished; this is “this and that cause.”

notes.dh: והא איפכא שמעינן להו ולד טריפה
notes.he: למ"ד טריפה יולדת ניחא דפליגי בזה וזה גורם אלא למ"ד אינה יולדת מוקמי פלוגתא פרק אלו טריפות (חולין נח.) בעובר ירך אמו ונתעברה ולבסוף נטרפה ומיהו אשכחן בעלמא דר' אליעזר סבר זה וזה גורם אסור ורבנן סברי מותר גבי שאור חולין ותרומה ושלהי כל הצלמים (ע"ז מט.) גבי נטל ממנה עצים אלא לרבי יהושע אייתיה ואע"ג דלאו דברי הכל הוא ומה שמזכיר כאן זה וזה גורם ופר' אותו ואת בנו (חולין עט:) נקט לישנא דחוששין לזרע האב משום דהכא איירי בדבר הבא מהיתר ואיסור [שייך שפיר] זה וזה גורם ומיהו קשה כיון דאין חוששין לזרע האב מאיזה טעם תחשב ולד טריפה זה וזה גורם לא יחשב שאור גורם וליתסר:
notes.en: But we have heard them say the opposite, the offspring of a tereifa: according to the one who says a tereifa can give birth, it is well: they disagree about “this and that cause.” But according to the one who says it cannot give birth, the dispute is set, in chapter Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 58a), where [the principle] “a fetus is its mother’s thigh” [applies], and it became pregnant and afterward became a tereifa. Yet we find elsewhere that Rabbi Eliezer holds “this and that cause” is forbidden and the Rabbis hold it is permitted: regarding leaven of non-sacred produce and of teruma, and at the end of Kol HaTzelamim (Avoda Zara 49a), regarding one who took wood from it [an ashera]. Rather, it is brought [here] for Rabbi Yehoshua, even though it is not everyone’s view. As for its speaking of “this and that cause” here, while in chapter Oto Ve’et Beno (Ḥullin 79b) it uses the expression “one is concerned about the seed of the father”: here it speaks of something that comes from the permitted and the forbidden, [so] “this and that cause” fits well. It is difficult, though: since one is not concerned about the seed of the father, for what reason should the offspring of a tereifa count as “this and that cause”? Let [the father] not count, so that the leaven [the forbidden element alone] causes it, and let it be forbidden.

notes.dh: והא איפכא שמעינן להו ולד טרפה
notes.he: אע"ג דאביו לאו טרפה אלא טהור שלם:
notes.en: But we have heard them say the opposite, the offspring of a tereifa: even though its father is not a tereifa but kosher and whole.

messages.text: The offspring may not be sacrificed upon the altar either, despite the fact that its father is kosher.
The offspring may be sacrificed upon the altar despite the fact that its mother is a tereifa, since its father is kosher.

Generally, Rabbi Eliezer holds that when both this and that cause the result, it is forbidden. But it is different here in the case of a kosher animal that became pregnant from a non-kosher animal, because if it is so, i.e., that the offspring is forbidden, let the verse write: Sheep and goats [seh kesavim ve’izzim]. Why do I need the verse to repeat the term “seh” in the phrase “seh kesavim veseh izzim”? Learn from it that a seh is permitted in any case, i.e., even if only the mother is kosher it is permitted to eat the offspring.

verse.he: זֹאת הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכֵלוּ שׁוֹר שֵׂה כְשָׂבִים וְשֵׂה עִזִּים׃
verse.en: These are the animals that you may eat: the ox, the sheep, and the goat;

notes.he: דעבורו מן הטמא אסור לכתוב שה כשבים ועזים:
notes.en: For if so: that [an offspring whose] conception was from a non-kosher animal is forbidden, let it write “seh kesavim ve’izzim.”

notes.he: למזבח אלמא דסבר ר' אליעזר זה וזה גורם אסור ור' יהושע סבר דמותר. לעולם בעלמא כגון לגבי מזבח סבר ר' אליעזר דזה וזה גורם אסור שאני הכא לגבי אכילה א"כ הוא דזה וזה גורם אסור לכתוב קרא שור כבשים ועזים דהוי משמע עד שיהא אביו ואמו כבש שה שה למה לי ש"מ שה מ"מ דזה וזה גורם מותר:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: it may not be sacrificed on the altar. Evidently Rabbi Eliezer holds “this and that cause” is forbidden, and Rabbi Yehoshua holds it is permitted. [The answer:] Actually, in general, as with regard to the altar, Rabbi Eliezer holds “this and that cause” is forbidden; here, with regard to consumption, it is different. If it were so that “this and that cause” is forbidden, let the verse write “ox, kesavim and izzim,” which would imply: until its father and mother are sheep. Why do I need “seh, seh”? Learn from it: a seh in any case, that “this and that cause” is permitted.

messages.text: And as for Rabbi Yehoshua, he could have said to you: Generally, if both this and that cause the result it is permitted. But here it is different, as if so, i.e., if the offspring of a kosher animal that became pregnant from a non-kosher animal is permitted, let the verse write: These are the animals that you may eat: An ox, a lamb, and a goat. Why do I need it to state: “Seh kesavim veseh izzim,” in the plural? Learn from it that the offspring may not be eaten unless its father is a male lamb and its mother is a female lamb.

messages.caption: “This and that cause”: each Tanna’s general rule, the case where it shows, and why the lamb is different.

messages.text: § Returning to the dilemma about Rabbi Shimon: Come and hear a proof from a baraita:

It is stated: “Camel”, “camel”, i.e., the term is written two times with regard to the prohibition against consumption. This teaches that both a camel that is born from a camel and a camel that is born from a cow are non-kosher. And if in the latter case its head and the majority of its body are similar to its mother, it is permitted for consumption.

verse.he: אַךְ אֶת־זֶה לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מִמַּעֲלֵי הַגֵּרָה וּמִמַּפְרִסֵי הַפַּרְסָה אֶת־הַגָּמָל כִּי־מַעֲלֵה גֵרָה הוּא וּפַרְסָה אֵינֶנּוּ מַפְרִיס טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם׃
verse.en: The following, however, of those that either chew the cud or have true hoofs, you shall not eat: the camel—although it chews the cud, it has no true hoofs: it is impure for you;

messages.text: Learn from it that not only with regard to firstborn status, but with regard to consumption as well Rabbi Shimon requires that its head and the majority of its body resemble the mother, and a partial resemblance does not suffice. Indeed, learn from it that this is so.
messages.quote: if its head and the majority of its body are similar to its mother, it is permitted for consumption

messages.text: This is because that which emerges from the non-kosher animal is non-kosher and that which emerges from the kosher animal is kosher.
With regard to the urine of a donkey, what is the halakha? Is it forbidden, like the milk of a donkey?
messages.lead: They raised a dilemma before Rav Sheshet:

messages.text: And should they raise the dilemma also with regard to the urine of horses and camels?

With regard to the urine of horses and camels they did not raise the dilemma, as their urine is not turbid and consequently is not similar to milk. Rather, water enters their body and water exits their body. When they raised the dilemma it was concerning the urine of a donkey, which is turbid and is consequently similar to milk. What is the halakha? Does it get excreted from its body, and it is therefore forbidden, or perhaps water enters and water exits, and the fact that it is turbid is due to the heat of the flesh?

notes.dh: מיא עול מיא נפוק והאי דעכירי הבלא דבישרא הוא
notes.he: מחמת חמימות וסרחון הבשר:
notes.en: Water enters, water exits, and that it is turbid is the heat of the flesh: due to the warmth and the putrefaction of the flesh.

notes.he: מה הן בשתיה. מיא עול מיא נפק. כלומר מים צלולים שתה מים צלולין מוציאין לפיכך מותרין:
notes.en: The urine of a donkey: what is [the law] regarding drinking it? Water enters, water exits: that is, it drank clear water and passes clear water; therefore they are permitted.

notes.he: האי דעכירו נימא משום הכי דמגופיה מאבריו קא מימצצי ואסירי דהוו כחלב שמתמצין מן הגוף ואסירי או דלמא אין מתמצצין אלא על מיא עול מיא נפיק והאי דעכירי משום הבליה מחמת חמימות הבשר הוא ומותרין שאינן מתמצצין מגופו:
notes.en: What: shall we say that, since it is turbid, it is squeezed from its body, from its limbs, and is forbidden, like milk, which is squeezed from the body and is forbidden? Or perhaps it is not squeezed [from the body], but water enters, water exits, and that it is turbid is due to its heat, the warmth of the flesh, and it is permitted, since it is not squeezed from its body?

messages.text: You learned the answer in the mishna: This is because that which emerges from the non-kosher animal is non-kosher and that which emerges from the kosher animal is kosher. From the fact that it does not state: That which emerges from a non-kosher animal [mittamei], meaning from the body of a non-kosher animal, but rather it says: From…
messages.quote: that which emerges from the non-kosher animal is non-kosher

notes.he: הוי משמע מגופיה דטמא מן הטמא משמע מינו של טמא הן דדמו לחלב:
notes.en: Mittamei would imply from the body of the non-kosher animal; min hattamei implies of the kind [min] of the non-kosher, that is, these, which resemble milk.

notes.he: דאי אמר הכי הוה משמע כל מה שיוצא מטמא בין עכירי בין לא עכירי:
notes.en: It does not say mittamei: for had it said so, it would imply everything that comes out of a non-kosher animal, whether turbid or not.

notes.he: קאמר כלומר הני דנפקי דהוו מין טמא דעכירי כמין חלב טמאין:
notes.en: Rather, it says min hattamei: that is, these that come out, which are a kind [min] of non-kosher substance, being turbid like a kind of milk, are non-kosher.

messages.text: 7b

…the non-kosher animal [min hattamei], one can infer that any type [min] of non-kosher substance is included. And these fluids, i.e., the urine of a donkey, are also a type of non-kosher substance, as they resemble the milk of a donkey, which is forbidden.

notes.he: מטמא קאתו שבתוך הטמא היו ואע"ג דלאו מגופיה מימצן אסירי:
notes.en: And these too: come from a non-kosher animal, for they were inside the non-kosher animal; and even though they are not squeezed from its body, they are forbidden.

messages.text: And there are those who say there is a different version of the discussion about the urine of a donkey:

With regard to the urine of horses and camels, the students of Rav Sheshet did not raise the dilemma, because people do not drink it. When they raised the dilemma it was with regard to the urine of a donkey, which people drink and which is beneficial for curing jaundice. What, then, is the halakha?

notes.dh: ואיכא דאמרי דסוסים וגמלים לא קא מיבעיא להו דלא שתו להו אינשי
notes.he: לשום רפואה ולא כלום הוי ולא אסיר דלא חשיבי למידי:
notes.en: And there are those who say that about horses and camels they did not ask, since people do not drink it for any remedy; it is nothing, and is not forbidden, since it is not significant for anything.

messages.text: You learned the answer to your dilemma in the mishna: That which emerges from the non-kosher animal is non-kosher and that which emerges from the kosher animal is kosher, and these fluids also come from a donkey, which is non-kosher. Therefore, they are forbidden.
messages.quote: the urine of a donkey, which people drink

notes.he: הא דמשמע לסימן נקטיה לא קשה מידי כדפרישי' לעיל (בכורות דף ו. ד"ה למה):
notes.en: You learned it: “that which emerges from the non-kosher is non-kosher.” That [the mishna’s wording] implies it was stated as a sign [an indicator] is no difficulty at all, as we explained above (6a, s.v. lamah).

notes.dh: כי קא מבעי' דחמור וכו' והני נמי מי רגלים של חמור מטמא קא אתו ואסירי
notes.he: להאי לישנא בתרא בין עכירי בין לא עכירי אסירי:
notes.en: When they asked, it was about a donkey, etc. And these too, the urine of a donkey, come from a non-kosher animal and are forbidden. According to this latter version, whether turbid or not, they are forbidden.

messages.text: For what reason did the Sages say that the honey of bees is permitted? It is because they bring the nectar from the flowers into their body, but they do not excrete it from their body as a bodily excretion.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita:

notes.he: שאוכלין מפרחי האילן ומהן נעשה הדבש במעיהן:
notes.en: That they bring it into their bodies: for they eat from the blossoms of the trees, and from them the honey is made in their innards.

notes.he: שיונקין אותו מעשבי ההרים:
notes.en: That they bring it into their bodies: for they suck it from the plants of the mountains.

messages.text: So too, the urine of a donkey is not an excretion produced by the body itself. Rather, it is simply ejected in the same form that it entered the body. Why, then, should it be forbidden?

notes.he: דובשנו מגופו וקשיא לרב ששת דהא הכא כיון דלאו מגופייהו מימצו שרי: רב ששת אמר כל שהיה בתוך הטמא דאמר כר' יעקב בטעמא דדבש לאו משום שמכניסות אותן לגופן הוא אלא דרחמנא שרייה בהדיא וגזירת הכתוב היא:
notes.en: And they do not squeeze it: their honey from their body. This is difficult for Rav Sheshet, for here, since it is not squeezed from their bodies, it is permitted. [Answer:] Rav Sheshet, who said that anything that was inside the non-kosher animal [is forbidden], spoke in accordance with Rabbi Ya’akov, for whom the reason for honey is not that they bring it into their bodies; rather, the Merciful One explicitly permitted it, and it is a decree of the verse.

notes.he: כשמוציאין אותן אלא כי היכי דעל הכי נפיק וקשיא לתרוייהו לישני ללישנא בתרא קשיא דהאי דבש דמטמא נפיק ושרי. וללישנא קמא קשיא דאילו התם קאמר כי עכירי אע"ג דלאו מגופיה ממיצצי אסירי והכא בדבש כיון דאין ממצות אותו מגופן שרי ורב ששת אמר לך בדבש שאני דאע"ג דמפיק ליה מגופיה שרי דהוא דאמר כר' יעקב דאמר דובשא כו':
notes.en: And they do not squeeze it from their bodies when they bring it out; rather, as it went in, so it comes out. This is difficult for both versions. For the latter version it is difficult, since this honey comes from a non-kosher creature and is permitted. For the first version it is difficult, since there it said that when they are turbid, even though they are not squeezed from its body, they are forbidden, while here with honey, since they do not squeeze it from their bodies, it is permitted. And Rav Sheshet would tell you: honey is different, for even if it comes from its body it is permitted, since he spoke in accordance with Rabbi Ya’akov, who said that honey, etc.

messages.text: Rav Sheshet stated his answer in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ya’akov, who says that with regard to honey, the Merciful One permits it as an exception to the principle that a substance that emerges from a non-kosher animal is non-kosher.
messages.quote: the honey of bees is permitted

messages.text: It is stated: “Yet these may you eat of all winged creatures”. The word “these” indicates that you may eat these, but you may not eat a non-kosher winged creature.
messages.lead: This is as it is taught in a baraita:

verse.he: אַךְ אֶת־זֶה תֹּאכְלוּ מִכֹּל שֶׁרֶץ הָעוֹף הַהֹלֵךְ עַל־אַרְבַּע אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) כְרָעַיִם מִמַּעַל לְרַגְלָיו לְנַתֵּר בָּהֵן עַל־הָאָרֶץ׃
verse.en: But these you may eat among all the winged swarming things that walk on fours: all that have, above their feet, jointed legs to leap with on the ground—

messages.text: Why is this inference necessary? The prohibition against eating a non-kosher winged creature is written explicitly: “All winged creatures that go upon all fours are a repugnance to you”.

verse.he: כֹּל שֶׁרֶץ הָעוֹף הַהֹלֵךְ עַל־אַרְבַּע שֶׁקֶץ הוּא לָכֶם׃
verse.en: All winged swarming things that walk on fours shall be an abomination for you.

notes.he: הוולד ממש בהדיא כתיב בו (ויקרא י״א:י״ג) את אלה תשקצו מן העוף:
notes.en: A non-kosher winged creature: the creature itself; [its prohibition] is written explicitly (Leviticus 11:13): “And these you shall hold in abomination among the birds.”

messages.text: Rather, the inference must be understood as follows: You may not eat a non-kosher winged creature, but you may eat that which a non-kosher winged creature discharges from its body, and what is that? That is the honey of bees.

notes.dh: אלא שרץ עוף טמא שאתה אין אוכל
notes.he: דלהכי דייקא ואי אתה דתיהדר ותידוק מיניה אבל אתה אוכל מה שעוף טמא משריץ שאינו ולד דוגמתו כגון דבש. ל"א אלא שרץ עוף טמא אי אתה אוכל ומאידך קרא נסיב לה מכל שרץ העוף וגו':
notes.en: Rather, a non-kosher winged creature you may not eat: for this is what it is precise to say, “and you may not,” so that you turn and infer from it: but you may eat what a non-kosher winged creature discharges that is not offspring like itself, such as honey. Another version: rather, a non-kosher winged creature you may not eat, and it derives it from the other verse, “All winged swarming creatures,” etc.

notes.he: שרץ עוף טמא בהדיא כתיב איסוריה אלא מאידך קרא מפיק ליה דכתיב את זה לא תאכלו שרץ עוף טמא אי אתה אוכל אבל אתה אוכל מה שעוף טמא משריץ מוציא מגופו:
notes.en: A non-kosher winged creature: its prohibition is written explicitly. Rather, he derives it from the other verse, as it is written, “these you shall not eat”: a non-kosher winged creature you may not eat, but you may eat what a non-kosher winged creature discharges, bringing it out of its body.

messages.text: One might have thought that even the honey of gizzin and wasps should be permitted. Nevertheless, you should say no.

notes.he: מין ארבה:
notes.en: Gizzin and wasps: a kind of locust.

notes.he: גרסינן ולא גרסינן חגבים שזה עוף כמו גזי דכלתא דנדה (דף יז.) לפי' ר"ת:
notes.en: Gizzin and wasps: this is our reading, and we do not read “locusts,” for this is a flying creature, like the gizzei dekhalta [mentioned] in Niddah (17a), according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam.

notes.he: מין ארבה:
notes.en: Gizzin: a kind of locust.

messages.text: And what did you see to include the honey of bees as being permitted to eat and to exclude the honey of gizzin and wasps as being forbidden? I include the honey of bees, as its name does not have a modifier, i.e., the word honey alone always refers to the honey of bees. And I exclude the honey of gizzin and wasps, which have a modifier, i.e., one must always add the word gizzin or wasp to specify these particular types of honey.

notes.he: דבש סתמא (הוו) קרו ליה. דבש הגזין הכי הוא דמיקרו:
notes.en: Bee honey: they call it simply “honey.” Gizzin honey is called by that [full] name.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is that which is taught in a baraita: The honey of gizzin and wasps is not susceptible to ritual impurity and is permitted for consumption? It is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ya’akov.

notes.he: מלקבל טומאת אוכלין דסתמיה לאו לאכילה עד שיחשב עליו:
notes.en: Pure: from contracting the impurity of food, since ordinarily it is not [meant] for eating until one intends it [as food].

messages.text: Is not susceptible to ritual impurity: apparently, in order for the honey of gizzin and wasps to become susceptible to ritual impurity it requires specific intention to eat it, which renders it food. Furthermore, the baraita indicates that honey from bees does not require specific intention to eat it in order for it to become susceptible, because it is normally used for food.
messages.quote: is not susceptible to ritual impurity

notes.he: בניחותא:
notes.en: Pure; evidently it requires intent: [read] as a statement [not a question].

notes.he: תולה שמו על שם שרץ האסור אלא דבש סתמא איקרי כדכתיב ביערת הדבש. מדאמרינן טהור אלמא בעי מחשבה דשאר דבש מטמא טומאת אוכלין אפי' שלא במחשבה והאי לא מטמא אי לא חישב עליו. הני חלי דיחמורתא שנמצאין ברעי שלה כעין ביצים סבור רבנן קמיה דרב ספרא למימר ביצי נינהו ואסירי באכילה דהוו כאבר מן החי דלא התירה [תורה] שום ביצים אלא דעוף [אבל אלו דומין] כביצים של בהמה שפורשין ממנה בחייה:
notes.en: That has no modifier: its name is not attached to that of the forbidden creature; rather, it is called simply “honey,” as it is written, “in the honeycomb” (I Samuel 14:27). Since we say “pure,” evidently it requires intent: for other honey imparts the impurity of food even without intent, and this does not, unless one intended it [as food]. [A note in the printed edition refers here to the Arukh, entry ḥali.] These ḥalei of the fallow deer, which are found in its excrement like eggs: the Sages before Rav Safra thought to say that they are eggs and forbidden for consumption, like a limb from a living animal, since the Torah permitted no eggs except those of birds, [and these resemble] the eggs of an animal that separate from it while it is alive.

messages.text: The honey of bees that is still in its hive is susceptible to ritual impurity as food even without intent.

notes.he: ואכתי לא חשיב עליה שהרי הוא בכוורתו. ובדבש דבורים מיירי דאין כוורת אלא לדבורים:
notes.en: Honey in its hive: and one has not yet intended it [as food], for it is still in its hive. It speaks of bee honey, for only bees have a hive.

messages.text: § With regard to chunks that are discharged from the womb of a female fallow deer, the Sages thought to say that they are its egg cells, and therefore are forbidden as a limb severed from a living animal.

notes.he: כעין ביצי זכר שהיחמורו' מוציאות מרחמן:
notes.en: Ḥalei of the fallow deer: something like male testicles, which female fallow deer discharge from their womb.

notes.he: משום אבר מן החי שנעקרו מן הזכר ברחם:
notes.en: And are forbidden: as a limb from a living animal, since they were torn from the male in the womb.

messages.text: It is the semen of a hart, which pursues the hind, but since the hind’s womb is narrow it does not mate with the hart, and instead the hart pursues the female fallow deer and mates with it, and chunks of its semen that have hardened fall out of the fallow deer’s body.

notes.he: להיזקק לה:
notes.en: That pursues the hind: to mate with it.

notes.he: שופך זרע הרבה ונקרש:
notes.en: And they fall out: it pours out much semen, and it congeals.

notes.he: אמר להו רב ספרא לאו ביצים נינהו אלא זרעא דאיילא הוא דאזיל בתר אילתא למיזקיק לה ולא מקבלא ליה אילתא משום דרחמה צר וכיון דחזיא דלא מקבלא ליה אזיל בתר שדומה לאיילא יחמורתא ועד שהוא הולך אחריה סובל בגופו שכבת זרעו ומתבשל בגופו הרבה וכשבא על היחמורה אגב דנתקרש הזרע הרבה אינו נבלע בגופה ומוציאתו לחוץ עם הריעי שלה ואותו זרע כיון שנתבשל נראה כעין ביצים ואינן ביצים ושרו דלאו כאבר מן החי נינהו:
notes.en: Rav Safra said to them: they are not eggs, but the semen of a hart, which goes after the hind to mate with it, and the hind does not accept it because her womb is narrow. When it sees that she does not accept it [a note in the printed edition: in the Arukh the reading is, it goes after the fallow deer, which resembles the hind], and while it pursues her, it carries its semen in its body, and it ripens there a great deal. When it mates with the fallow deer, since the semen has congealed a great deal, it is not absorbed in her body, and she discharges it with her excrement. That semen, since it has ripened, looks like eggs, but it is not eggs, and they are permitted, for they are not like a limb from a living animal.

messages.text: The skin that emerges opposite the face of a donkey when it is born, i.e., the fetal sac that envelopes it during birth, is permitted to be consumed. What is the reason? It is merely a secretion, and is not an integral part of the mother or the offspring.

notes.he: כעין שליא שהחמור נולד בו:
notes.en: The skin that emerges opposite the face of a donkey: something like an afterbirth in which the donkey is born.

notes.dh: עור הבא נגד פניו של חמור
notes.he: פי' כדלעיל:
notes.en: The skin that emerges opposite the face of a donkey: explained as above.

notes.he: עור הבא כנגד פניו של חמור מותרין באכילה שכשנולד החמור יש לו עור דק על פניו כעין שליא ולאו שליא הוא ואינו דבוק נמי לפניו אלא כך הוא בריה בפני עצמו ופירשא בעלמא הוא:
notes.en: The skin that emerges opposite the face of a donkey is permitted for consumption: when a donkey is born it has a thin skin over its face, like an afterbirth, but it is not an afterbirth, nor is it attached to its face; rather, it is a creation of its own and merely a secretion.

messages.text: @Rav Huna That which is taught in a baraita supports your opinion:

notes.he: דפירשא בעלמא הוא:
notes.en: A baraita supports you: that it is merely a secretion.

messages.text: The skin that emerges opposite the face of a person, i.e., a newborn baby, whether the newborn is alive or dead, is ritually pure and does not transmit ritual impurity imparted by a corpse.

notes.he: מלטמא במגע ובמשא:
notes.en: Pure: from imparting impurity by touch and by carrying.

notes.dh: עור הבא כנגד פניו של אדם
notes.he: דהכי נמי יש לאדם עור דק על פניו כשנולד ואותו עור אינו לא מן האם ולא מן הולד וטהור הוא משום טומאת מת:
notes.en: The skin that emerges opposite the face of a person: for a person too has a thin skin over his face when he is born, and that skin is neither from the mother nor from the offspring, and it is pure with regard to corpse impurity.

messages.text: What, is it not the case that whether it is alive and its mother is alive or whether it is dead and its mother is dead, it is not considered a part of the body of the fetus or the mother, but merely a secretion, and therefore even when they are both dead it does not transmit impurity?

notes.he: אפילו הולד והאם מתים אפ"ה העור אין מטמא אלמא דאמר שליא לא מן הולד ולא מן האם אלא פירשא בעלמא היא:
notes.en: What, is it not: even when the offspring and the mother are dead, even so the skin does not impart impurity. Evidently he holds that the afterbirth is neither from the offspring nor from the mother, but is merely a secretion.

notes.dh: מאי לאו בין הוא ואמו מתה
notes.he: פי אלמא לא הוי העור לא מן הולד ולא מן האם אלא הזרע שנתקדש:
notes.en: What, is it not whether it [is dead] and its mother is dead: explanation: evidently the skin is neither from the offspring nor from the mother, but is the seed that hardened [the printed word, nitkadesh, apparently stands for a word meaning “congealed”].

messages.text: No, there is no proof from this baraita, as it may mean that whether it is alive and its mother is dead or whether it is dead and its mother is alive, meaning only one is alive, the skin is ritually pure. But if both are dead it is impure.
messages.quote: whether it is dead and its mother is dead

notes.dh: ה"ג לא בין הוא חי ואמו חיה בין הוא מת ואמו חיה
notes.he: שמגוף האם הוא והרי היא חיה אבל לגבי אכילה כי שדית ליה בתר אם נמי אסור:
notes.en: This is the reading: “No: whether it is alive and its mother alive, or it is dead and its mother alive” [Rashi’s text thus differs from the Davidson English, which reads “alive and its mother dead … dead and its mother alive”]: for it is from the body of the mother, and she is alive. But with regard to consumption, when you assign it to the mother, it is also forbidden.

notes.dh: לא בין הוא חי ואמו מתה בין הוא מת ואמו חיה
notes.he: שהעור בא בין שניהם מן האם ומן הולד ולפיכך טהור עד שימותו שניהם ובקונטרס פירש כך בין הוא ואמו חיה בין הוא מת ואמו חיה [אבל] אמו חיה לעולם בעינן וכמו שפיר' נראה דמדנקט רב חסדא בין הוא מת ואמו מתה משמע דאין לו סייעתא אלא מהא דמטהרינן בשניהם מתים אבל אם האחד חי אין כאן סייעתא:
notes.en: No: whether it is alive and its mother dead, or it is dead and its mother alive: for the skin comes from between the two of them, from the mother and from the offspring, and therefore it is pure until both of them die. In the Kuntres [Rashi] explained it thus: “whether it and its mother are alive, or it is dead and its mother alive,” [so that] its mother’s being alive is always required. But what we explained seems right, since Rav Ḥisda’s saying “whether it is dead and its mother is dead” implies that his support comes only from our ruling it pure when both are dead; if one of them is alive, there is no support here.

notes.dh: לא בין הוא חי ואמו מתה
notes.he: דשדינן ליה בתר חי הא לאו הכי מטמא:
notes.en: No: whether it is alive and its mother is dead: for we assign it to the living one; otherwise it imparts impurity.

messages.text: But isn’t it taught in a baraita that whether it is alive and its mother is alive or whether it is dead and its mother is dead, the skin is pure?
@Rav Ḥisda If this baraita is taught, it is taught, and I cannot dispute it.

notes.he: והתניא בין הוא מת ואמו מתה טהור אי תניא תניא:
notes.en: But isn’t it taught: whether it is dead and its mother is dead, it is pure? If it is taught, it is taught.

messages.text: Mishna
In the case of a non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish, consumption of the kosher fish is permitted.

notes.he: משמע דידעי ודאי שבלעו:
notes.en: Mishna. That swallowed: implies that we know for certain that it swallowed it.

messages.text: And in the case of a kosher fish that swallowed a non-kosher fish, consumption of the non-kosher fish is prohibited due to the fact that the host fish is not the place of its development.

notes.he: אלא כשהוא חי בלעו אבל גידוליו שרי שהיוצא מן הטהור טהור:
notes.en: Since it is not its growth: rather, it swallowed it alive. But what grows within it is permitted, for what emerges from the kosher is kosher.

notes.dh: דג טהור שבלע דג טמא אסור באכילה
notes.he: תימה במסכת אהלות (פי"א מ"ז) תנו כלב שאכל בשר המת כמה תשהה במעיו שלשה ימים מעת לעת ובעופות ובדגים כדי שתפול לאור ותשרף אלמא חשיב עכול והכא נמי לישתרי ולא מסתבר לחלק בין בשר המת לשאר דברים דשלשה ימים דכלב משמע בכל דבר דמדמייתי עלה במסכת שבת פרק השואל (דף קנה:) יודע הקב"ה בכלב שמזונותיו מועטות לפיכך משהה אכילתו במעיו שלשה ימים ויש לחלק בין איסור לטומאה ויש רוצים להתיר מתוך משנה זו חטה שנמצאת בפסח במעי תרנגולת ולפי מה שחלקתי בין איסור לטומאה אין זה ראיה עוד פירש ר"ת דשמא יש להחמיר כר' יהודה בן בתירה דבעי מעת לעת ואם באנו לומר דאין חילוק בין איסור לטומאה צ"ל דשמעתא אתיא בלא שהה כדי עיכול וא"ת אי לא שהה כדי עיכול היכי פריך בגמ' כי חזינא דבלע נימא האי איעכל והאי אשרוצי אשריץ י"ל פעם ממהר להתעכל קודם ולא הוי ככלב דלעולם ג' ימים:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot ask why a non-kosher fish swallowed by a kosher one is forbidden, given the mishna in Oholot (11:7): a dog that ate corpse flesh imparts impurity for three full days, but in birds and fish, only as long as it takes to fall into a fire and be burned; evidently what a fish swallows counts as digested at once, so here too it should be permitted. One cannot distinguish corpse flesh from other foods, since the dog’s three days apply to everything, as Shabbat (155b) explains: the Holy One knows that a dog’s food is scarce, so He keeps its food in its innards three days. One may instead distinguish between prohibition and impurity. Some want to use this mishna to permit a grain of wheat found on Passover inside a chicken; with the distinction between prohibition and impurity, that is no proof. Rabbeinu Tam adds that perhaps one should be stringent like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, who requires a full day. And if there is no distinction between prohibition and impurity, our passage must speak of a fish that did not stay long enough to be digested. If so, how can the Gemara say “that one was digested and this one it spawned”? Sometimes it is digested sooner; a fish is not like a dog, whose time is always three days. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: Gemara

The reason consumption of the kosher fish is permitted is that we saw that the non-kosher fish swallowed the kosher fish. But if we did not see it swallow the kosher fish we say that perhaps the non-kosher fish spawned the kosher fish, and it is forbidden.
messages.quote: a non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish

notes.he: דג טהור זה שנמצא בתוך הטמא נשרץ בגופו ועוברו הוא ואסור:
notes.en: Gemara. It spawned it: this kosher fish found inside the non-kosher one was spawned in its body and is its fetus, and it is forbidden.

notes.dh: טעמא דחזיניה לדג טמא דבלע דג טהור
notes.he: משום הכי מותר באכילה הא לא חזיניה דבלע אמרינן אשרוצי אשריץ כלומר דהא דג טמא איעבר להאי דג טהור במעיו:
notes.en: The reason is that we saw the non-kosher fish swallow the kosher fish: therefore it is permitted for consumption. But if we did not see it swallow, we say it spawned it; that is, the non-kosher fish was pregnant with this kosher fish in its innards.

messages.text: From where do we derive that we must have this concern? As it is taught in a baraita:
A non-kosher fish spawns offspring, while a kosher fish lays eggs from which the offspring hatch.

notes.he: בגופו עוברו כשאר בהמה וחיה:
notes.en: A non-kosher fish spawns: [it carries] its fetus in its body, like other domesticated and undomesticated animals.

notes.he: ויושב עליהן ומחממן עד שיוציאם מן הקליפה כעופות:
notes.en: A kosher fish lays eggs: and sits on them and warms them until it brings them out of the shell, like birds.

notes.he: מתעבר ומוליד וולדותיו:
notes.en: As it is taught, a non-kosher fish spawns: it becomes pregnant and gives birth to its young.

notes.he: דג טהור מטיל ביצים ומחממן עד שיש בהן צורה ובוקען ויוצאין:
notes.en: A kosher fish lays eggs and warms them until they take form, and breaks them open, and they come out.

messages.text: If so, even when we saw it swallowing a kosher fish we should say that that fish that it swallowed was digested, and this one, which was found inside of the non-kosher fish, it spawned, and should be forbidden.

notes.he: דדג טמא משריץ האי דבלע איעכל והוי ריעי וזה שנמצא בתוכו אשרוצי אשריציה ועוברו הוא וליתסר:
notes.en: If so: since a non-kosher fish spawns, [say that] the one it swallowed was digested and became excrement, and this one found inside it, it spawned; it is its fetus, and let it be forbidden.

notes.he: האיך דבלע איעכלא במעיו והאי דנמצא במיעיו אשרוצי אשרוציה וליתסר:
notes.en: That one which it swallowed was digested in its innards, and this one found in its innards it spawned; and let it be forbidden.

messages.text: It is referring to a case where one found the kosher fish in the digestive tract, which is not where the non-kosher fish normally spawns its offspring.

notes.he: ואי עוברו הוא בבית הרחם מיבעי ליה לאישתכוחי:
notes.en: In the digestive tract [literally, the passage of excrement]: and if it were its fetus, it should be found in the womb.

notes.he: להאי דג טהור דרך בית הרעי דטמא דאם איתא דאשרצי לא משתכח בבית הרעי אלא בשילייתו. או שמצא בבית הבליעה שאין דרכו של וולד להיות שם. או שמצאו שלם דאם איתא דהוי דולד לא הוה שלם גמור אלא ודאי בלעו:
notes.en: For example, where he found this kosher fish in the non-kosher one’s digestive tract: for if it had spawned it, it would not be found in the digestive tract but in its afterbirth. Or he found it in the passage of swallowing, where young are not normally found. Or he found it whole: for if it were its young, it would not be fully whole; rather, it certainly swallowed it.

messages.text: Similarly: it is referring to a case where one found the kosher fish in the passageway of the gullet.
It is referring to a case where one found it whole and in complete form, and not as a newly hatched fish.

notes.he: שנגמרה כל צורתו וגדול הוא ואי עוברו לא הוי משתהי ברחם כולי האי:
notes.en: That he found it whole: its whole form is complete and it is large; and if it were its fetus, it would not stay in the womb that long.

messages.text: Do not infer from the mishna that it is referring to a case where the non-kosher fish was seen swallowing the kosher fish. Rather, the reason it is permitted to consume the swallowed fish is that the majority of fish spawn offspring of their own species, and therefore the case of a kosher fish discovered inside a non-kosher fish is considered as if the non-kosher fish had swallowed the kosher fish in our presence.

notes.he: מתני' לאו כדחזיניה דבלע אלא שנמצא בתוכו והאי דקתני שבלע כיון דרוב דגים במינן משריצים וזה השריץ מין אחר כמו שבלע בפנינו דמי:
notes.en: Rav Ashi says: [he understands] the mishna not as where we saw it swallow, but where it was found inside it. And it teaches “that swallowed” because most fish spawn their own species, and this one [would have] spawned another species, so it is as if it swallowed it in our presence.

notes.he: הלכתא כרב אשי דהוא בתראה ויש להתיר אותן דגים שקורין מרנ"ש הנמצא תוך דג בלינ"א ואע"ג דלא חזינן דבלע ואין להקשות ממתני' דשריא דג טמא שבלע דג טהור לרב ששת דאסר מי רגלים של חמור דאפי' ללישנא בתרא דרב ששת דאסר אף של סוסים וגמל לא דמי חדא דמתני' לא איירי אלא נמצא תוכו דג טהור ואפילו יצאו הכא פשיטא דדגים עייל דגים נפיק אבל מים שהבהמה שותה לחלוחית הגוף מתערב עמהם ובת"כ תני גבי דגים תאכלו לרבות הטהור שבמעי טמא יכול אף הטמא שבמעי טהור ת"ל אותם מה ראית לומר בבהמה שבמעי טמא טמא ושבמעי טהור טהור (מטמא שבמעי הטהור טהור) ובדגים אינו כן לפי שאין גדוליו ואין ראיה משם לאסור דג טמא שבלע דג טהור אחר שיצא משום דנקט שבמעי הטמא דלאו דוקא אלא משום טמא שבמעי טהור דדילמא ההיא דשרינן ביצא לחוץ משום דחשיב עיכול:
notes.en: In brief: The halakha follows Rav Ashi, the latest authority, so one may permit the fish called marenes found inside the fish called blina (Tosafot give the Old French names), even though we did not see it swallow. Nor is our mishna, which permits a kosher fish swallowed by a non-kosher one, a difficulty for Rav Sheshet, who forbids a donkey’s urine, even in the version that forbids that of horses and camels too: the mishna speaks of a kosher fish found inside, and it is obvious that fish go in and fish come out, whereas the water an animal drinks mixes with the moisture of its body. Torat Kohanim teaches about fish: “You shall eat” includes the kosher fish in a non-kosher fish’s innards; might the non-kosher in a kosher one’s innards be included too? The verse says “them.” Why? With animals, what is in a non-kosher animal is non-kosher and what is in a kosher animal is kosher; with fish it is not so, since it is not its growth. That passage gives no proof for forbidding a kosher fish swallowed by a non-kosher one once it has come out: “in the innards of the non-kosher” was said only because of the non-kosher one in the innards of the kosher, and perhaps the case it permits is where it came out, since it is considered digested. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: רב אשי אמר כיון דרוב דגים טמאין במינן משריצין מולידין ולא מין אחר והאי כיון דטהור הוא שנמצא בבטנו כמי שבלע בפנינו דוודאי דג טמא אינו משריץ אלא מינו:
notes.en: Rav Ashi says: since most non-kosher fish spawn, that is, give birth to, their own kind and not another kind, and this one found in its belly is kosher, it is as if it swallowed it in our presence, for certainly a non-kosher fish spawns only its own kind.

messages.text: A non-kosher fish spawns its offspring, while a kosher fish lays eggs. Any animal that gives birth to its offspring nurses them, and any animal that lays eggs gathers food and feeds it to its young. This applies to all animals except for a bat [atallef], as although it lays eggs, it nurses its young.
messages.lead: § The Gemara cites the entirety of the previously mentioned baraita. The Sages taught:

notes.he: שיולד עובר ממש:
notes.en: Any that gives birth: that bears an actual fetus.

notes.he: שיש לו דדים וכל המטיל ביצים אין לו דדים ומלקט פירורים ומפרנס בניו:
notes.en: Nurses: it has teats; and any that lays eggs has no teats, and it gathers crumbs and sustains its young.

notes.he: עטלף קלב"א שורי"ץ דומה לעכבר ויש לו כנפים:
notes.en: Atalef: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss, calve soriz, “bat.”) It resembles a mouse and has wings.

notes.dh: דג טמא משריץ דג טהור מטיל ביצים
notes.he: בע"ז פרק אין מעמידין (עבודה זרה דף מ.) מפרש תרוייהו מטילי ביצים נינהו זה משריץ מבחוץ וזה משריץ מבפנים:
notes.en: A non-kosher fish spawns, a kosher fish lays eggs: in Avoda Zara, chapter Ein Ma’amidin (40a), it explains that both of them lay eggs; this one spawns outside, and that one spawns inside.

notes.he: כל המוליד מניק ולדותיו וכל המטיל ביצים מלקט ביצים ויושב עליהן ומחממן ובכך פרה ורבה. ואיכא דאמר מלקט שאינו מניק אלא מלקט המאכל בפיו וזרקו לפני ולדותיו ובכך מפרנסן:
notes.en: Any that gives birth nurses its young, and any that lays eggs gathers the eggs, sits on them and warms them, and thereby is fruitful and multiplies. And some say “gathers” means that it does not nurse but gathers food in its mouth and throws it before its young, and thereby sustains them.

messages.text: The baraita continues on 8a: the dulfanin reproduce like people.
